title: Constructible underlying sets of module sheaves with finite stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ any commutative ring. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], constructible in the sense of [def-constructible-constructible]. Suppose every geometric stalk over a separably closed field [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is finite as a set. Then the sheaf of sets obtained by forgetting the module structure first to abelian groups and then to sets is constructible in the finite-set stratification sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ or finiteness hypothesis on $\Lambda$ is required.

source.place: Constructibility of the middle term; step 1 underlying-set construction of lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-finite-stalk-module; agent-formulated generalization of the finite prime-field case

proof.text: Retain the module constructible stratification. Forgetting each locally constant module datum yields a locally constant set datum on each stratum. Import all Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ConstructibleModuleUnderlyingSets and use its existing private underlyingSetPullbackIso, without redeclaring it, to compare set inverse image with the underlying set sheaf of module inverse image. This comparison has no finite-coefficient-ring hypothesis.

Use the inverse-image geometric-fiber isomorphism to identify each module stalk on a stratum with the corresponding source stalk. The point-ulift sheaf-fiber isomorphism handles the hypothesis universe. Forgetting commutes with the geometric fiber, since it preserves filtered colimits. Thus every underlying set stalk on every stratum is finite. Transport these facts through the inverse-image comparison, producing the desired set stratification. Empty strata cause no exception.
